title: Routine experimental access to microbial dark matter

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a generalizable workflow that turns discovery of a previously inaccessible microorganism into a maintained culture suitable for experiments. It would identify and supply the environmental conditions, nutrients, growth factors and microbial partners needed for growth, then support repeated propagation and physiological investigation. Here, microbial dark matter refers to microbial lineages whose existence can be detected but whose biology remains difficult to investigate directly through cultivation.

Sequencing would help identify target organisms, track their responses to cultivation conditions and guide changes to those conditions. Genome-derived metabolic predictions can inform this process, but frequently leave important requirements unresolved. A successful workflow would connect those predictions with experimental evidence about growth and dependencies. Access could include defined co-cultures when an organism requires partners, provided the target can be maintained and its behavior investigated.

significance.text: If reproducible across diverse habitats and previously inaccessible lineages, this capability would substantially expand the organisms available for direct experimental microbiology. Maintained cultures allow researchers to measure physiology, test inferred metabolic functions and investigate responses under controlled conditions. Effective genetic or other causal perturbations would further allow experiments that establish which biological mechanisms produce an observed behavior. The supplied evidence supports this conditional experimental-access argument without quantifying how much additional diversity could become accessible.

As a downstream possibility, access to additional organisms could reveal drugs, enzymes and useful biological processes. Each application would require subsequent discovery, validation and development. The revolutionary scope therefore depends on sustained, experimentally useful access across lineages and habitats. A cultivation improvement confined to one bacterial order demonstrates a narrower advance, and the supplied bacterial results leave equivalent access to other microbial groups unresolved.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unsolved capability is a dependable discovery-to-culture process that generalizes across organisms with substantially different biological requirements. Concrete barriers include identifying suitable growth conditions from incomplete biological knowledge, supplying required growth factors, and preserving dependencies that isolation can disrupt. The reviewed article discusses possible helper organisms and cross-feeding requirements as explanations for cultivation difficulties. Those explanations remain hypotheses for particular failed cultures unless tested directly.

Initial growth must also be converted into sustained propagation. Organisms detected in plate microcolonies may fail during subculture, so a discovery workflow needs methods for identifying what changed between initial growth and subsequent transfer. For partner-dependent organisms, this includes determining which community members or exchanged resources must persist. The supplied evidence establishes the subculture problem while leaving its causes unresolved for many affected organisms.

An additional engineering requirement, proposed here, is to make recovered organisms usable for repeatable experiments. That entails reliable maintenance procedures, controlled handling of necessary partners and effective physiological or causal interventions. Generalization would require these capabilities to work across a predefined range of habitats and lineages with practical costs and effort. The supplied study establishes portions of the cultivation pathway, while broad experimental accessibility remains the intended capability.

current_state.text: The supplied 2024 Nature Communications study by Minjia Zheng, Linran Wen, Cailing He and colleagues profiled bacterial cultivability in soil and activated sludge using sequencing-based assessment. Its targeted isolation and growth-enhancement demonstrations used activated-sludge-derived material. This distinction matters when interpreting habitat breadth, because profiling both sample types provides broader observational coverage than the targeted cultivation demonstrations.

In material from an enhanced biological phosphorus removal bioreactor, sequencing-guided cultivation recovered EBPR01, reported as the first isolate of the previously uncultured class c_JABWAT01 within Bacteroidota. The authors obtained the isolate after picking approximately 60 colonies and described streak purification and genomic classification. This demonstrates experimental access to a representative of an additional bacterial class, with broader recovery and maintenance across that class still unestablished.

Vitamin B12 supplementation increased detectable cultivable diversity within Burkholderiales in two additional sludge samples. Diversity was assessed through amplicon sequence variants, or ASVs, detected on plates. Enhanced growth increased sequencing detection, so the result concerns the diversity detectable under the tested conditions. Establishment and maintenance of every additionally detected lineage were not demonstrated.

The study reported that a substantial portion of bacteria in microcolonies ceased growing during subculture, without a numerical fraction supplied in the review. It also distinguished cultivable taxa from cultivable cells. Colony counts alone therefore provide an incomplete measure of recovered taxonomic diversity. Sequencing depth further affects that assessment, and some taxa detected on plates were absent from the corresponding inoculum sequencing results, making the starting-diversity denominator uncertain.

The supplied review covered the complete 15-page main article. Referenced supplementary materials were absent from that reviewed copy, which limits assessment of details available only in those materials. The record contains no assessment of subsequent literature through 1 November 2026, so these dated findings establish a demonstrated baseline while leaving later field progress unresolved.

completion_criteria.text: A proposed convincing demonstration would have independent laboratories apply an affordable, reproducible workflow to preselected samples from several habitats. They would recover and maintain a substantial, independently assessed fraction of previously inaccessible lineages, including partner-dependent organisms. Before evaluation, investigators would specify habitat coverage, the definition of previous inaccessibility, taxonomic resolution, recovery thresholds, maintenance duration or transfer requirements, and affordability limits. These are proposed evaluation criteria requiring operational definitions.
completion_criteria.label: Independent labs recover and maintain inaccessible lineages across habitats

completion_criteria.text: Recovery should be measured against the organisms present in the starting samples, with taxon-based results reported alongside cell or colony measurements. Investigators would report sequencing depth, detection limits and uncertainty in the denominator, including how they handle organisms detected after cultivation that were missed in inoculum sequencing. Initial plate growth, successful isolation and continued maintenance would each need explicit measurement because the reviewed study demonstrates that these outcomes can diverge.
completion_criteria.label: Recovery measurements report starting-sample denominators and distinct cultivation outcomes

completion_criteria.text: A further proposed demonstration would establish physiological experiments and genetic or other causal perturbations on a predefined representative subset of recovered organisms. For co-cultures, experiments would need sufficient control to attribute effects to the target, its partners or their interaction. Reproducibility would include independent recovery, maintenance and experimental use, with failures and practical requirements reported. Finite trials would establish the breadth demonstrated across the tested organisms and habitats, while broader generalization would remain an empirical question.
completion_criteria.label: Recovered organisms support reproducible physiological experiments and causal perturbations

related_concepts.text: Conceptual synthesis places MIC-03 at the intersection of culturomics, comparative genomics, community ecology and experimental genetics. MIC-02, A predictive theory of microbial communities, could help identify growth dependencies and suitable partners, while recovered cultures would provide systems for testing community predictions. MIC-10, Programmable microbial consortia for durable ecosystem functions, shares the need to maintain interacting organisms, with its central objective focused on engineered collective function.

MIC-01, An autonomously reproducing cell built from defined components, and MIC-06, A predictive whole-cell model for microbial design, share an interest in experimentally tractable cells. MIC-03 seeks access to existing microbial lineages. MIC-01 concerns constructing a reproducing cell, and MIC-06 concerns predicting cellular behavior for design. Additional cultures could supply comparative experiments and model-validation systems while leaving those separate construction and prediction challenges to be solved.

MIC-04, Reliable nitrogen-fixing microbial partnerships for major cereal crops, and MIC-07, Programmable, reversible living therapies in the human microbiome, could benefit from access to previously inaccessible partner organisms. Their completion would additionally require reliable function in plant-associated or human-associated environments, respectively. MIC-12, A causal map from microbial metabolites to host phenotypes, overlaps through the need for controlled microbial experiments, with host-level causal attribution adding a further requirement.

MIC-05, A general platform for targeted, adaptable phage treatment, could benefit from cultivating additional bacterial hosts and testing their phage interactions. MIC-08, Broadly effective control of bacterial antibiotic persistence, could use expanded culture access to investigate survival mechanisms across more organisms. MIC-09, Forecasting horizontal gene transfer and resistance spread in microbial communities, could gain experimental systems for measuring transfer. Each retains its distinct treatment, control or forecasting objective.

MIC-11, Quantifying how environmental viruses control biogeochemical fluxes, overlaps through access to microbial hosts and controlled host–virus experiments. Such cultures could support mechanistic measurements, while ecosystem-scale flux attribution would require additional environmental evidence and quantitative integration. These relationships are conceptual interpretations of the supplied roster.

unresolved_issues: Subsequent progress through 1 November 2026 remains unassessed because no freshness research was supplied.
Referenced supplementary materials were absent from the reviewed copy, leaving details dependent on those materials unassessed.
The achievable fraction of previously inaccessible diversity, its variation across habitats and extension beyond bacteria remain unresolved.
The causes of individual subculture failures, including specific helper or cross-feeding requirements, require targeted experiments.
Sequencing detection limits leave uncertainty in the starting-sample denominator, especially for taxa detected only after cultivation.
Affordability, substantial recovery, maintenance duration and representative experimental coverage require predefined thresholds before the proposed completion criteria can be evaluated.

brief.title: Growing elusive microbes for routine experiments
possible: Researchers could grow and repeatedly study microbes that they can currently detect but struggle to keep alive in the lab. A dependable process would find the food, conditions and microbial partners each needs, then keep it growing through repeated transfers.
why: This would open more of microbial life to direct experiments. Researchers could measure how these organisms live, test predictions from their genes and change specific biological processes to find out what causes their behavior.
Access to more microbes could also reveal drugs, enzymes and useful biological processes.

sources.who: Minjia Zheng, Linran Wen, Cailing He and colleagues
sources.showed: They used DNA readings to guide cultivation and recovered a bacterium from a previously uncultured broad bacterial group. Adding a vitamin also increased the bacterial variety detectable on growth plates.
sources.quote: some of them cease to grow during subculture.
sources.cited_for: DNA-guided cultivation can recover elusive bacteria, but initial growth does not guarantee continued growth.
sources.not_established: They did not establish reliable recovery and maintenance across diverse habitats and microbial groups.

sources.who: Yiming Huang, Ravi U. Sheth and colleagues
sources.showed: They built a robotic system that uses colony images and genetic information to select bacteria for cultivation. It produced gut bacterial collections containing over 26,000 isolates, or separately grown strains.
sources.quote:
Application of this ML model led to an improvement in targeted isolation  
of microbes of interest.
sources.cited_for: Automation and software that learns from data can make cultivation faster and recover a wider variety of bacteria.
sources.not_established: Large gut bacterial collections do not establish dependable access to previously inaccessible microbes across habitats.

sources.who: Pallavi P. Murugkar, Andrew J. Collins, Tsute Chen and Floyd E. Dewhirst
sources.showed: They established stable cultures of human oral Saccharibacteria, a group of bacteria that depend on bacterial hosts, by growing them together with suitable hosts.
sources.quote: Complete genome sequences were obtained for 16 isolates.
sources.cited_for: Keeping necessary host bacteria can turn otherwise inaccessible microbes into maintained cultures.
sources.not_established: Success with these oral bacteria does not establish a general method for finding and preserving microbial dependencies.

sources.showed: They grew an insect-associated bacterium with its host. Blocking its hair-like surface structures reduced movement, host attachment and growth.
sources.quote: We further showed that the inhibition of T4P extrusion suppressed the motility and host adherence of TM7i, resulting in its reduced growth.
sources.cited_for: Cultivation with a host can enable experiments that test how a dependent bacterium attaches and grows.
sources.not_established: This result does not establish reproducible experiments across a representative range of recovered microbes.

sources.showed: They grew environmental microbes inside tiny gel droplets supplied with dilute nutrients. The droplets allowed molecules to pass between neighboring microbes.
sources.quote:
The encapsulated microorganisms were
able to divide and form microcolonies
sources.cited_for: Conditions closer to the natural environment can support growth that conventional cultivation misses.
sources.not_established: Growth in droplets does not establish dependable continued cultivation and experimental use across microbial diversity.

shown: Researchers have achieved separate parts of the goal. Zheng and colleagues recovered a representative of a previously uncultured bacterial group. Huang and colleagues automated large gut bacterial collections. Murugkar’s and Xie’s teams maintained host-dependent bacteria, and Xie’s team tested a mechanism involved in host attachment.
missing: A dependable, affordable process has yet to recover and maintain diverse inaccessible microbes across habitats in independent labs.
Initial growth still needs to become reliable continued growth, including preservation of essential microbial partners.
Recovery measurements need to distinguish initial growth, isolation and maintenance against the diversity in the starting sample.
Recovered microbes need to support repeatable experiments that identify causes, with partner effects kept distinguishable.

milestones.label: Independent labs recover and maintain microbes across habitats
milestones.explanation: Independent labs would have to affordably recover and maintain a substantial share of inaccessible groups, including partner-dependent ones, across preselected habitats. Agreed criteria would establish the breadth and reliability achieved.

milestones.label: Recovery measurements distinguish starting diversity and cultivation outcomes
milestones.explanation: Measurements would have to compare recovered groups with starting diversity, account for detection limits, and separate initial growth, isolation and maintenance. This would reveal how much lasting access cultivation actually delivers.

milestones.label: Recovered microbes support repeatable experiments that establish causes
milestones.explanation: A predefined representative subset would have to support independently repeatable experiments on function and cause, with effects attributable to targets, partners or their interaction. This would establish usable experimental access.

uncertain: How much inaccessible diversity can become experimentally usable, and how does that vary across habitats and beyond bacteria?
Which missing nutrients, partners or other changes explain individual failures after transfer to fresh growth conditions?
What recovery share, maintenance period, experimental coverage and cost would count as sufficient?

page.title: Cultivation of microbial dark matter
page.definition: A cultivation workflow recovers bacteria and archaea known from environmental DNA but lacking cultures, termed microbial dark matter, as cultures that grow through repeated transfers. It preserves identified microbial partners when required and enables controlled experiments on cellular functions.

goal.need: Huang and colleagues’ study, published on 20 February 2023, generated 26,997 bacterial isolates from 20 human faecal donors. Coverage of each donor’s microbiota remained incomplete and depended on pooling isolates across donors. Maintained cultures allow controlled experiments on physiological functions inferred from genomes.

figures.caption: Bacterial sequence abundance represented by cultured isolates across 20 donors
figures.note: Coverage weights bacterial 16S marker-sequence variants by their abundance in each donor’s faecal sample. It is not the percentage of species recovered.

statements.quote: Microbiology needs to move beyond its dependence on pure cultures of organisms and appreciate the value of defined but mixed communities.
improved subcultivation, purification, and preservation techniques to recover and utilize a larger fraction of microbial diversity.
statements.context: Research recommendation in a review by DSMZ researchers Jörg Overmann, Birte Abt and Johannes Sikorski.

statements.body: U.S. Department of Energy Joint Genome Institute
statements.quote: Link Genomes to Phenotypes for Uncultured Microbes and Consortia

completion.title: Independent laboratories reproduce cultivation and experimental access across habitats and domains.
completion.criterion: Independent laboratories reproduce one discovery-to-culture workflow for previously uncultivated bacteria and archaea, covering environmental and host-associated samples. Recovered organisms persist through repeated transfers to fresh medium, alone or with identified partners, and support controlled physiological perturbation experiments. Replication includes recovery from source samples and confirmation of target identity after transfer.
completion.basis: Searches of American Academy of Microbiology recommendations, DSMZ’s cultivation roadmap, DOE JGI’s strategic plan, ICNP culture-deposit rules, and cultivation benchmark and prize rules found no general completion test specifying recovery breadth, maintenance, experimental access and independent replication together. This provisional test combines the published goals of maintained cultures, defined partners and experimental characterization without assigning an unsupported recovery percentage or cost limit.

milestones.title: Previously uncultivated microbes divide and form microcolonies under laboratory conditions.
milestones.criterion: Cells from a previously uncultivated lineage divide and form microscopically detectable colonies. In Zengler and colleagues’ paper dated 26 November 2002, environmental cells formed microcolonies of approximately 20–100 cells in permeable gel droplets. After five weeks, 1,200 microcolony-containing droplets were sampled from each of four media. Six recovered microcolonies were affiliated with a previously uncultivated alphaproteobacterial lineage.
milestones.set_by: Zengler and colleagues, published gel-microdroplet cultivation protocol; microscopy and flow cytometry established initial growth.
milestones.threshold_quote: The encapsulated microorganisms were able to divide and form microcolonies

milestones.title: A recovered bacterial colony reaches an optical density above 0.05 after 14 days in fresh medium.
milestones.criterion: In Zheng and colleagues’ subculture assay, a picked colony is transferred to corresponding liquid medium without agar, incubated for 14 days, and scores successful if optical density at 600 nm exceeds 0.05. The study published on 20 October 2024 tested 26 microcolonies and 22 macrocolonies; most microcolonies failed subculture. Separately, sequencing-guided picking of approximately 60 colonies yielded streak-purified EBPR01, the first isolate assigned to Bacteroidota class c_JABWAT01.
milestones.set_by: Zheng and colleagues, Methods: Examinations on microcolonies. This is their bacterial liquid-subculture assay, not a universal cultivation threshold.
milestones.threshold_quote: Turbidity was measured, and cases where the optical density at 600 nm wavelength exceeded 0.05 were considered successful for subculture.

milestones.title: A previously uncultivated microbe persists in an identified culture through serial transfers.
milestones.criterion: The target persists through successive transfers to fresh medium, alone or with identified partners, and its identity is confirmed after transfer. In the paper published on 1 December 2022, Xie and colleagues recovered one insect-associated Saccharibacteria strain, TM7i, with Leucobacter aridicollis J1. TM7i persisted through multiple broth and agar passages and was verified by target-specific PCR. The protocol does not specify a universal minimum transfer count.
milestones.set_by: Xie and colleagues, published epicPCR-directed isolation protocol; serial passage and PCR validation were specified for Saccharibacteria–host cultures.
milestones.threshold_quote: recovery of CPR‒host symbionts by serial passage and PCR validation.

milestones.title: A recovered microbe exhibits a physiological response in a controlled perturbation experiment.
milestones.criterion: A recovered culture supports a defined intervention with a measured physiological response and corresponding controls. Xie and colleagues’ TM7i–J1 growth assay used 50, 100 or 200 μM quercetin and solvent controls, with three biological replicates per group. TM7i growth decreased with dose, while J1 growth was not significantly affected. Microscopy also showed reduced TM7i motility at 200 μM and recovery after quercetin removal.
milestones.set_by: Xie and colleagues, TM7i motility and growth-assay protocols, Figures 3–4. These pharmacological tests were developed for this Saccharibacteria–host pair.
milestones.threshold_quote: T4P inhibition with quercetin blocks twitching motility and host infection.

milestones.title: A recovered prokaryote is available alive from two public collections in different countries.
milestones.criterion: A recovered prokaryote has viable type-strain cultures deposited in at least two publicly accessible collections in different countries that can supply the strain. This is the ordinary ICNP deposit requirement; specified exceptions exist. The code recognizes host cocultures. One example is the archaeon Nanobdella aerobiophila MJ1, catalogued as JCM 33616 in Japan and DSM 111728 in Germany, maintained with Metallosphaera sedula MJ1HA.
milestones.set_by: International Committee on Systematics of Prokaryotes, ICNP 2025 Revision, Rules 18a and 30(3)(b), published in 2026. The requirement concerns type-strain deposition.
milestones.threshold_quote: a viable culture of that strain must be deposited in at least two culture collections in different countries

milestones.title: One laboratory establishes maintained experimental cultures across habitats and prokaryotic domains.
milestones.criterion: One laboratory applies one discovery-to-culture workflow to previously uncultivated bacteria and archaea spanning environmental and host-associated samples. Recovered targets remain identifiable through serial transfers, support controlled physiological perturbation experiments, and are available as living cultures through public collections. The cited studies establish components of this outcome; a demonstration combining them across the stated breadth was not located.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas; provisional step before independent replication. Searches of academy recommendations, cultivation roadmaps and agency plans found no published test combining these outcomes across habitats and domains.

not_found: No external completion standard was located that specifies recovery breadth, maintained cultivation, experimental access and independent replication together.
No independently replicated workflow combining those outcomes across environmental and host-associated bacteria and archaea was located.
Murugkar and colleagues’ 2020 full article could not be reopened through PMC or its publisher.

results.finding: Cultured TM7x: quercetin-treated cells had a mean twitching speed of 0.02 μm/second (N=20).
results.detail: TM7x was maintained with its bacterial host. The motility assay used 200 μM quercetin and a DMSO vehicle control; untreated wildtype cells averaged approximately 0.22 μm/second (N=58).
results.quote: Because the T4P inhibitor quercetin inhibited twitching (0.02 μm/second), and loss of T4P-2 did not, our data indicate that T4P-1 likely drives twitching motility.
